reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised
reviews.text: I downloaded this app and subscribed to the free trial. Then I forgot about it and accidentally purchased the year subscription… I AM SO GLAD THAT HAPPENED!! I figured I might as well give it an honest try since I’ve paid for the year and it’s seriously been a godsend. I’m a full time working mom of three, my husband is in school, I’m starting grad school soon, and I was spending hours a week meal planning, making grocery lists, grocery shopping and stressing the whole time about staying under budget. With this app I can do it all in minutes, the meals are all super good and easy to make. My kids, all 6 and under, have enjoyed every single meal and they’re being exposed to types of food we haven’t eaten much of before. I feel like I’ve been hunting my whole adult life for recipes like these. I’ve already told everyone that will hear me about the app. It’s one thing to take off the mental load of having to meal plan but it also saves me money, saves me time, and is yummy and nutritious. If I could give it 10 stars I would.

reviews.title: Needs more personalization
reviews.text: App is a great concept but needs more preferences. The “won’t eat” section is very limited right now. For people with 0 picky eaters in the family, the app is great. However, for those who have picky eaters and/or those allergic to certain foods, it needs some work. Won’t eat section should include a lot more things like won’t eat “dark meat, pork, peanuts, shell fish (or other allergy related foods). Also maybe include a healthy section like only lean meats, low fat diets etc. I get it, the app is new and designed to save money at the store. But again it doesn’t work too well for picky eaters and allergic people. (I myself am not a picky eater and I can’t control what a kid likes/doesn’t like or what people are allergic to).

reviews.title: Great concept but...
reviews.text: There are a lot of things I like about this app! I came to this app from Mealime (RIP 🙏 (IYKYK)) and it has a lot of similar features that are cool (like building a shopping list based on my meal plan) and even some things that are better (e.g. being able to add things to my kitchen/pantry so they don't show up in my list every week)! That said, I do take issue with some of the recipes. So far I've made 3-4 recipes from TapCook and idk if they're written by AI or what but the steps often do not make sense; it feels to me like steps are often missing, out of order, or incompatible with each other. The food tastes good but the process is tough and sometimes leads to mistakes that could be avoided if the instructions were clearer. So I guess I would say: this app is good if you know enough about cooking to identify errors/inconsistencies in the recipes and adjust accordingly but if you are new to cooking maybe give it a pass and find something with better directions.

reviews.title: Perfect for bland meals
reviews.text: It did its job. Created a budget menu. Unfortunately they need to invest in expanding their recipe offerings. 2 weeks of the most bland, unappealing, chicken nugget kid type dinners that literally made me cancel. Nothing unique. Just breaded pork cutlets, pork cutlet either gravy, crusted pork cutlet like what the heck? No offerings of any Mexican, Italian, Indian dinners. I wanted the ease of not having to break my brain in half to provide delicious meals but I guess you have to sacrifice flavor as well. Maybe they could invest in better recipes to attract a wide clientele. Actually do some market research and talk to real moms of different cultures to see the budget friendly meals we make at home that also incorporate a ton of flavor. Offer that in your onboarding. Allow clients to select cuisine preferences like Mediterranean, Mexican, Italian, etc. and ACTUALLY provide those recipes. Maybe I’ll come back in a year when they’ve garnered more attention and offerings.

reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.text: The only complaint I have at this point is that the recipes don’t have any preparation steps for the ingredients. For example it just says, “fry bok choy stems then leaves.” How should the bok choy be cut? Sliced in half, chopped? I had to reference the picture to find out. Also, it asks for salt, but never reminds you to add it during the cooking steps. Now, I know how to cook, but I imagine some newbie forgetting and getting bland steak. I think the devs could easily add the preparation steps, or at least descriptions of the desired form in the line for each ingredient. I assume these are mostly AI recipes anyway, so it shouldn’t be that hard.

reviews.title: Could you some tweaking
reviews.text: Overall, this is a great app and has truely helped me be less wasteful and save money at the grocery store. I have found that the pricing isn’t accurate though. It’s close enough on the veggies and pantry items but it’s always way off on the meats. I’d love if meats were the price that this app showed them to be! I would love if this app had the option to show you where to cheapest place to get the items was vs just choosing where you shop. It would also be neat if it offered multiple meal choices, for example me and the kiddos eat most all of the things and our diets aren’t restricted, my husband eats keto/carnivore. It would be super sweet if it allowed me to do both!

reviews.title: Game changer!
reviews.text:
This is my first ever rating of an app on the App Store! I am not a good cook, and I have never really enjoyed cooking. I’ve tried so many ways to get into cooking more whole food meals while also being conscious of what we spend on groceries. This is the first time I’ve felt like I found a real solution! I can’t believe how easy this app is from start to finish. 
The recipes and meals we’ve had so far have been delicious and pretty easy and straightforward. I’m so excited to continue discovering new foods and cooking regularly! The yearly subscription cost is well worth it in my opinion.

reviews.title: Everything done for you, except the cooking!
reviews.text:
This app is wonderful. Making a grocery list from the items you do not have in your home is great, but giving you the option to order the grocery list…thats next level. I like the variety of meals, it is going to be interesting to try out. I also like that I can swap out any meal for another of my choosing. Great job TapCook!

My only critique would be to add an option for a pickup order from your store of choice. I would rather pick them up front the store than have them delivered to me.

reviews.title: Life Saver
reviews.text:
This app is amazing!  I’m a busy mom who appreciates all of these tasks combined in one app. I did EveryPlate for years and grew tired of the meals going bad because they were too many steps and I didn’t have time. These recipes are delicious, quick, easy and healthy!  The shopping budget flexibility and store selection is so helpful. And the fact that it tells you how to store your food and fill in what you already have. 
I would love the flexibility to move the days around in case something happens and I need to change up.

reviews.title: VERY Disappointed
reviews.text: Do not waste your money on this app. This app, I believe, is not fully developed before promoting it to the public. First, it says you get a free seven day trial… well that was false. I ended up having to pay right upfront when I thought I was getting a free trial. Next, after paying that’s when you can see what meals you can get for the week, well because I chose Paleo as the diet, I was only given three meals in total. It said because of my diet, I am not able to access 18 other meals. Which is not even enough meals to get somebody through two weeks or three weeks and the three meals that I can only eat would only cover one days worth. This app is not good, and it took my money after false promotion. Don’t even waste your time. I want a refund. This is poor development.
